prs.title: fix(core): enforce maxTotalTimeout without progress notifications
prs.author: claxman
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs modify the same request-timeout state machine in packages/core-internal/src/shared/protocol.ts that governs how `timeout` and `maxTotalTimeout` interact — specifically the code path that (re)arms the per-request timer, including on progress-notification resets. #2763 fixes the root cause (the initial timer arm ignored `maxTotalTimeout` entirely, so a hung call with no progress notifications waited the full `timeout` instead of the shorter `maxTotalTimeout`), and its changeset explicitly describes the full intended behavior including how progress-triggered resets should re-arm against the remaining budget. #2817 touches the progress-reset function itself and makes `info.startTime` update to `Date.now()` on every reset. That is incompatible with #2763's fix: if `maxTotalTimeout` is enforced by comparing elapsed time against a fixed original `startTime`, resetting `startTime` on every progress notification means the elapsed-time clock never accumulates, so `maxTotalTimeout` could never actually fire as long as progress notifications keep arriving — defeating the hard-cap guarantee #2763 is adding. They are two overlapping/conflicting fixes to the same underlying timeout-accounting bug rather than independent changes. (2 PRs)

members.title: fix(core): enforce maxTotalTimeout without progress notifications
members.author: claxman
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs modify the same request-timeout state machine in packages/core-internal/src/shared/protocol.ts that governs how `timeout` and `maxTotalTimeout` interact — specifically the code path that (re)arms the per-request timer, including on progress-notification resets. #2763 fixes the root cause (the initial timer arm ignored `maxTotalTimeout` entirely, so a hung call with no progress notifications waited the full `timeout` instead of the shorter `maxTotalTimeout`), and its changeset explicitly describes the full intended behavior including how progress-triggered resets should re-arm against the remaining budget. #2817 touches the progress-reset function itself and makes `info.startTime` update to `Date.now()` on every reset. That is incompatible with #2763's fix: if `maxTotalTimeout` is enforced by comparing elapsed time against a fixed original `startTime`, resetting `startTime` on every progress notification means the elapsed-time clock never accumulates, so `maxTotalTimeout` could never actually fire as long as progress notifications keep arriving — defeating the hard-cap guarantee #2763 is adding. They are two overlapping/conflicting fixes to the same underlying timeout-accounting bug rather than independent changes. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: #2763 ships a changeset covering all three affected packages (core-internal, client, server) as required for a patch release, and its diff plus changeset describe the complete fix: capping the initial timer at min(timeout, maxTotalTimeout), re-arming against the remaining budget on progress resets, and raising the 'Maximum total timeout exceeded' error on cap expiry. #2817 has no changeset at all, only touches the progress-reset function with a one-line `info.startTime = Date.now()` change plus a test-comment tweak, and that change conflicts with maintaining a fixed original start time — which is what a remaining-budget calculation against maxTotalTimeout depends on. Landing #2817 alongside or instead of #2763 would re-introduce a way to bypass the hard cap via repeated progress notifications.

members.title: fix(core): enforce maxTotalTimeout without progress notifications
members.author: claxman
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs modify the same request-timeout state machine in packages/core-internal/src/shared/protocol.ts that governs how `timeout` and `maxTotalTimeout` interact — specifically the code path that (re)arms the per-request timer, including on progress-notification resets. #2763 fixes the root cause (the initial timer arm ignored `maxTotalTimeout` entirely, so a hung call with no progress notifications waited the full `timeout` instead of the shorter `maxTotalTimeout`), and its changeset explicitly describes the full intended behavior including how progress-triggered resets should re-arm against the remaining budget. #2817 touches the progress-reset function itself and makes `info.startTime` update to `Date.now()` on every reset. That is incompatible with #2763's fix: if `maxTotalTimeout` is enforced by comparing elapsed time against a fixed original `startTime`, resetting `startTime` on every progress notification means the elapsed-time clock never accumulates, so `maxTotalTimeout` could never actually fire as long as progress notifications keep arriving — defeating the hard-cap guarantee #2763 is adding. They are two overlapping/conflicting fixes to the same underlying timeout-accounting bug rather than independent changes. (2 PRs)
